description: Re-run all 9 metacognition benchmarks against all 10 Bedrock models for final submission numbers
steps: Step 1: Activate venv: source repo/.venv/bin/activate
Step 2: Run python3 repo/scripts/run_benchmark_bedrock.py with track=metacognition for all 10 models (parallelism <=4 to avoid OOM)
Step 3: Collect results from results/{model_id}.json for all 9 metacog benchmarks: canary, calibration, control, epistemic_humility, epistemic_revision, error_detection, fok, jol, learning_monitoring
Step 4: Build updated score matrix at results/metacog_final_scores.csv (columns: benchmark, model, score, duration_s)
Step 5: Compute per-benchmark stats (mean, std, range) and verify avg std >= 0.10
Step 6: Flag any regressions vs KNOWLEDGE baselines

description: Polish metacognition writeup with updated 10-model results from the final Bedrock run
steps: Step 1: Read results/metacog_final_scores.csv generated by the re-run task
Step 2: Open repo/WRITEUP_METACOGNITION.md and update all score tables with fresh 10-model numbers
Step 3: Update the Results section with: per-benchmark mean/std/range, top and bottom model per benchmark, and the three-tier pattern stats (Tier 1 vs Tier 2 vs Tier 3 means)
Step 4: Verify word count stays <= 1500 words using wc -w
Step 5: Save the updated writeup

description: Generate a cover image for the metacognition writeup submission
steps: Step 1: Create a Python script that generates a publication-quality figure showing the three-tier metacognition pattern across models

Step 2: Use matplotlib to create a grouped bar chart: x-axis = 9 benchmarks grouped by tier (External Monitoring / Self-Monitoring / Prospective Self-Assessment), y-axis = score (0-1), bars = top 3-5 most interesting models
Step 3: Add tier labels and a horizontal dashed line at human baseline where available
Step 4: Save as repo/assets/metacognition_cover.png at 1200x800px, 150 DPI
Step 5: Verify the image renders correctly by checking file size > 50KB

description: Validate all 9 metacognition benchmark notebooks match their latest task_*.py implementations
steps: Step 1: For each of the 9 benchmarks, diff the core logic in repo/notebooks/metacog_*.ipynb against repo/benchmarks/metacognition/task_*.py
Step 2: Check that scoring formulas, item counts, and prompt templates match between notebook and .py file
Step 3: Run jupyter nbconvert --to notebook on each of the 9 notebooks to verify syntax
Step 4: List any mismatches found with specific line numbers and describe what needs syncing
Step 5: Fix any mismatches by updating the notebook cells to match the .py source of truth

description: Create discriminatory analysis summary table for metacognition track writeup
steps: Step 1: Load results/metacog_final_scores.csv (or results/score_matrix.csv if final not yet available)
Step 2: For each of the 9 metacog benchmarks compute: mean score, std, range, coefficient of variation, and rank the benchmarks by discriminatory power (std)
Step 3: Identify the top-3 most discriminating benchmarks and bottom-3 least discriminating
Step 4: Generate a markdown table saved to results/metacog_discriminatory_summary.md with columns: Benchmark, Mean, Std, Range, CV, Top Model, Bottom Model
Step 5: Write a 2-3 sentence interpretation paragraph below the table suitable for pasting into the writeup
